title: The 10 Best Narrow Crown Staplers
subtitle: 18-gauge pneumatic and cordless narrow crown staplers, ranked from live Amazon data.
intro: A narrow crown stapler drives 1/4-inch crown staples that hold thin panels and trim backing better than brads. We ranked 10 best-sellers from Metabo HPT, BOSTITCH, Makita, Senco, CRAFTSMAN, RYOBI and value brands on rating, review volume and features (depth adjustment, a selectable trigger, a case, dry-fire lockout and a no-mar tip).
data_source: Amazon product listings on the data_captured date. Prices, ratings and review counts change daily; check the listing before relying on a number.

avoid.name: POPULO 2-in-1 Pneumatic Brad Nailer and Crown Stapler (ABN-5040)
avoid.flag: Calls an 18-gauge brad nailer a finish nailer
avoid.verdict: A 2-in-1 brad nailer and stapler that markets itself as a finish nailer for crown molding and door casing, jobs an 18-gauge brad isn't meant to hold.
reasons: It calls itself an 'ideal finish nailer', but it shoots 18-gauge brads. Finish nailers use thicker 15- or 16-gauge nails.
It lists crown molding and door casing as uses. 18-gauge brads have little holding power for heavy trim like that.
The model number (ABN-5040) and part number (ABE-5040) don't match. The WEN 61722K is the same kind of 2-in-1 with a case and an honest description.

buyers_guide.q: What's a narrow crown stapler for?
buyers_guide.a: 18-gauge narrow crown staples (1/4-inch crown) hold better than brads in thin material: cabinet backs, drawer bottoms, upholstery frames, trim backing and underlayment.
Pick staples about 2-1/2 times the thickness of the material you're fastening. Most staplers take 1/2 to 1-1/2 or 1-5/8 inch staples.
Sequential fires one staple per trigger pull for accuracy. Contact (bump) fires when you press the nose down with the trigger held, which is faster for production work.
2-in-1 tools shoot brads and staples, good for DIYers. Dedicated staplers are lighter and more reliable for heavy use.
Pneumatic staplers are lighter and cheaper but need a compressor. Cordless ones go anywhere but are heavier and cost more.
